newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, Chernomyrdin to discuss summit, IMF.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, Chernomyrdin to discuss summit, IMF.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, recovering from pneumonia, will meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday at his country residence outside Moscow, the presidential press service said on Tuesday.

Yeltsin's spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told Interfax news agency the two men would discuss the details of the Russia-U.S. summit in Helsinki next month, Russia's relationships with the International Monetary Fund and budget problems.

They would focus their talks on a new tranche of the IMF loan to Russia, Yastrzhembsky said. The IMF board on Friday approved disbursement of more than $650 million from its $10 billion loan to Russia.
Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin and Chernomyrdin would also discuss the results of Chernomyrdin's meetings with U.S. President Bill Clinton and Vice-President Al Gore in the United States last week.

Yeltsin, 66, has held a series of one-on-one meetings since he was taken ill with pneumonia last month, but he has not attended public gatherings or large meetings. He was absent from the Kremlin for most of the second half of last year with heart problems.
